q.t: Indirect: Riya said, “I am tired.”
o: Riya said that she was tired.
Riya said that I am tired.
Riya said that she is tired.
Riya told that she was tired.
q.e: I → she; am → was (one step back); joiner ‘that’.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “I like ice cream.”
o: He said that he liked ice cream.
He said that I liked ice cream.
He said that he likes ice cream.
He said me that he liked ice cream.
q.e: I → he; like → liked.

q.t: Which reporting verb needs a person after it?
o: told
said
exclaimed
replied
q.e: We ‘tell someone’ but simply ‘say’. So: told me, said that.

q.t: Indirect: She said, “I will come.”
o: She said that she would come.
She said that she will come.
She said that I would come.
She said that she comes.
q.e: will → would.

q.t: In indirect speech, tomorrow usually becomes:
o: the next day
yesterday
today
that tomorrow
q.e: Your ‘tomorrow’ is not theirs, so it becomes ‘the next day’.

q.t: In indirect speech, here becomes:
o: there
where
this
now
q.e: The speaker’s ‘here’ is ‘there’ for the person retelling it.

q.t: Indirect: The teacher said, “Sit down.”
o: The teacher told us to sit down.
The teacher said that sit down.
The teacher told us that we sit down.
The teacher told us sit down.
q.e: Orders → told/ordered + person + to + V1.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “I can swim.”
o: He said that he could swim.
He said that he can swim.
He said that I could swim.
He told that he could swim.
q.e: can → could.

q.t: Indirect: Mother said, “Don't go out.”
o: Mother told me not to go out.
Mother told me don't go out.
Mother said me not to go out.
Mother told me to not going out.
q.e: Negative command → told + person + not to + V1.

q.t: What joiner is used for a yes/no question?
o: if / whether
that
to
what
q.e: Yes/no questions are reported with if or whether.

q.t: Indirect: He said to me, “Where do you live?”
o: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where do I live?
He said me where I lived.
q.e: Use the wh-word as joiner, statement order (I lived), no ‘do’, no question mark.

q.t: Indirect: She said to him, “Are you hungry?”
o: She asked him if he was hungry.
She asked him if was he hungry.
She asked him are you hungry.
She asked him that he was hungry.
q.e: Yes/no question → if/whether + statement order; you → he; are → was.

q.t: Indirect: Ravi said, “I have finished my work.”
o: Ravi said that he had finished his work.
Ravi said that he has finished his work.
Ravi said that he finished my work.
Ravi said that I had finished my work.
q.e: have finished → had finished; I → he; my → his.

q.t: Indirect: She said, “I saw a snake.”
o: She said that she had seen a snake.
She said that she saw a snake yesterday.
She said that she has seen a snake.
She said that I had seen a snake.
q.e: Simple past → past perfect: saw → had seen.

q.t: Indirect: The teacher said, “The earth goes round the sun.”
o: The teacher said that the earth goes round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth went round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had gone round the sun.
The teacher said the earth is going round the sun.
q.e: A universal truth does not change tense — it is still true.

q.t: Indirect: She says, “I am busy.”
o: She says that she is busy.
She says that she was busy.
She said that she was busy.
She says that I am busy.
q.e: The reporting verb ‘says’ is present, so no backshift.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “Please lend me your pen.”
o: He requested me to lend him my pen.
He requested me to lend me your pen.
He said please to lend him my pen.
He requested me that lend him my pen.
q.e: Request → requested + person + to + V1; me → him; your → my.

q.t: Indirect: She said, “I am going to the market today.”
o: She said that she was going to the market that day.
She said that she is going to the market today.
She said that she was going to the market today.
She said that she went to the market that day.
q.e: am going → was going; today → that day.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “I met her yesterday.”
o: He said that he had met her the day before.
He said that he met her yesterday.
He said that he had met her tomorrow.
He said that he has met her the day before.
q.e: met → had met; yesterday → the day before.

q.t: Indirect: The boy said, “I may be late.”
o: The boy said that he might be late.
The boy said that he may be late.
The boy said that he could be late.
The boy said that I might be late.
q.e: may → might.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “What a beautiful garden!”
o: He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful garden.
He said that what a beautiful garden.
He exclaimed what a beautiful garden it is.
He asked what a beautiful garden it was.
q.e: Exclamations → exclaimed that + a statement with ‘very’.

q.t: Indirect: She said, “Alas! I have lost my purse.”
o: She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
She said alas that she had lost her purse.
She exclaimed with joy that she had lost her purse.
She exclaimed with sorrow that I had lost my purse.
q.e: ‘Alas’ shows sorrow → exclaimed with sorrow; have lost → had lost.

q.t: Indirect: He said to me, “Did you call me?”
o: He asked me if I had called him.
He asked me did I call him.
He asked me if I called me.
He asked me that I had called him.
q.e: Yes/no → if; did call → had called; you → I; me → him.

q.t: Indirect: The guard said to us, “Don't park here.”
o: The guard told us not to park there.
The guard told us not to park here.
The guard told us don't park there.
The guard said us not to park there.
q.e: Negative command → not to + V1; here → there.

q.t: Indirect: She said, “I will meet you tomorrow.”
o: She said that she would meet me the next day.
She said that she will meet me tomorrow.
She said that she would meet you tomorrow.
She said that I would meet her the next day.
q.e: will → would; you → me (the listener is the one retelling); tomorrow → the next day.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “Good morning, sir.”
o: He wished his teacher good morning.
He said good morning sir.
He said that good morning, sir.
He told that it was a good morning.
q.e: Greetings are reported with ‘wished’.

q.t: Indirect: The doctor said to me, “You should rest.”
o: The doctor advised me to rest.
The doctor ordered me rest.
The doctor said me that I should rest.
The doctor advised me that rest.
q.e: Advice → advised + person + to + V1 (or ‘told me that I should rest’).

q.t: Direct form of: She asked me what my name was.
o: She said to me, “What is your name?”
She said to me, “What was my name?”
She said to me, “What is my name?”
She said, “What your name is?”
q.e: Reverse the changes: was → is, my → your, and the question order comes back.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “These books are mine.”
o: He said that those books were his.
He said that these books are his.
He said that those books were mine.
He said that these books were his.
q.e: these → those; are → were; mine → his.

q.t: Indirect: She said, “I must leave now.”
o: She said that she had to leave then.
She said that she must leave now.
She said that she has to leave then.
She said that I had to leave then.
q.e: must → had to; now → then.

q.t: Indirect: The old man said, “May God bless you!”
o: The old man prayed that God might bless me.
The old man said that may God bless me.
The old man wished that God bless you.
The old man exclaimed God may bless him.
q.e: Wishes and blessings → prayed/wished that … might.

q.t: Indirect: He said, “Let's go for a walk.”
o: He suggested that we should go for a walk.
He told let's go for a walk.
He said that let us go for a walk.
He ordered us to go for a walk.
q.e: ‘Let's’ is a suggestion → suggested that we should …

q.t: Indirect: She said to him, “Why are you crying?”
o: She asked him why he was crying.
She asked him why was he crying.
She asked him why he is crying.
She asked him that why he was crying.
q.e: wh-word as joiner, statement order: he was crying.

q.t: Indirect: The captain said, “Well done, boys!”
o: The captain applauded the boys, saying that they had done well.
The captain said that well done boys.
The captain told well done to boys.
The captain exclaimed that boys done well.
q.e: Praise is reported with ‘applauded/praised’ and the meaning is turned into a statement.

q.t: Find the error: She asked me where was I going.
o: ‘was I going’ should be ‘I was going’
‘asked’ should be ‘said’
‘me’ should be ‘I’
No error
q.e: In indirect questions the order goes back to statement order.

q.t: Find the error: He said me that he was busy.
o: ‘said me’ should be ‘told me’
‘was’ should be ‘is’
‘that’ should be ‘if’
No error
q.e: ‘said’ never takes a person directly; use ‘told me’ (or ‘said to me’).

q.t: Direct form of: He told me not to touch the switch.
o: He said to me, “Don't touch the switch.”
He said to me, “Not touch the switch.”
He said to me, “You didn't touch the switch.”
He said, “I don't touch the switch.”
q.e: ‘not to + V1’ comes from a negative command: Don't …

q.t: Indirect: He said, “I have been working here for two years.”
o: He said that he had been working there for two years.
He said that he has been working there for two years.
He said that he had been working here for two years.
He said that he was working there for two years.
q.e: have been working → had been working; here → there.

q.t: Indirect: She said to me, “Shall I open the window?”
o: She asked me if she should open the window.
She asked me if she shall open the window.
She asked me that should she open the window.
She told me to open the window.
q.e: An offer with shall → asked if … should.

q.t: Indirect: The teacher said to Riya, “Thank you for your help.”
o: The teacher thanked Riya for her help.
The teacher said thank you Riya.
The teacher told Riya that thank you for help.
The teacher thanked to Riya for your help.
q.e: ‘Thank you’ is reported as ‘thanked + person’; your → her.
